conviction_note: Scaled: abs_move 17 (option-implied 15.84, own median 13.4, a full FY27 outlook due on this call, history understates) x p_up 58 = +2.72. The lean is long because module-maker and contract-DRAM series for Jun-Aug run well above what the July guide implied for Memory and pricing kept rising into Sep-Nov (MU guided above, TrendForce 4Q26 +10-15%), and this name has paid on guidance raises (+25%, +13%) and been sold on holds (-14%). p_up is held to 58 because the skew (-23.7, upside bid), the 15.7% 20-day run-up and the +11.6% Oct-2 pop on 'expects a raise' mean much of a raise is in the price. impact_sum is +4.4 against a scaled +2.72; the gap is that p_up discounts the priced half while the per-finding sizes do not.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 (Jun-Aug) Memory revenue is tracking above the July guide: the guide (Memory +90-95% FY on FY25 $464.2M, 9M $583.3M) implies Q4 Memory $299-322M (+9% to +17% QoQ from $275.1M), while TrendForce contract DRAM rose 58-63% in Apr-Jun and 13-18% in Jul-Sep (Jun-Aug average ~+25% over Mar-May), and module maker ADATA's Jun-Aug revenue was NT$51.97bn vs NT$34.04bn in Mar-May (+52.7% QoQ); at +25% QoQ Memory alone is ~$345M, putting total Q4 near $540-550M vs the $519.3M consensus, though gross margin % is diluted by pass-through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (Jul 2026): Memory +111% YoY, +60% QoQ, EPS $0.84 vs $0.63, with a raise: +25.13%. Q1 FY26 (Jan 2026): memory-driven quarter with full-year guide held at 6%: -13.78%. The reported quarter alone has not carried this stock; the guide has.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus $519.3M sits only ~$12M above the guide midpoint and ~$16M below its top, i.e. the street has Memory up ~15% QoQ; if it had priced the contract and module-maker series, revenue estimates would cluster at or above the $535M top of the guide rather than spanning $507-541M. Calibration: in Q3 the same price arithmetic (~+67% Dec-Feb to Mar-May) matched Penguin Memory's reported +60% QoQ.
findings.independence: Two series, different sources: TrendForce contract prices (https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260703-13134.html, 2026-07-03; Q2 +58-63% per https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260407-13001.html) and ADATA monthly revenue (https://finance.technews.tw/2026/09/07/adata-3260-202608-financial-report/, https://technews.tw/2026/07/06/adata-3260-202606-financial-report/, https://finance.technews.tw/2026/06/08/adata-3260-202605-financial-report/, https://finance.technews.tw/2026/04/07/adata-3260-202603-financial-report/). Both are proxies: ADATA is channel/spot-heavy and Penguin is data-center, LTA-capped CSPs are not Penguin's customers. Company itself: 'very strong backlog entering the 4th quarter' (same PDF).

findings.finding: The full FY27 outlook due on this call has room to exceed the July 7 preliminary ~+30% (sales ~$2.17B, EPS ~$3.38, which equals current consensus EPS), because memory pricing kept rising after it was set: TrendForce's late-September 4Q26 call is conventional DRAM +10-15% QoQ with RDIMM undersupply into 2027, Micron on Sept 30 guided FQ1-27 revenue $61.5B and EPS $38.15, both above estimates, and Dell (Penguin's AI compute partner, named 2026 Americas AI Partner of the Year) reported traditional servers +122% and a $95B AI backlog; the prelim also explicitly excludes hyperscale AC hardware and the Penguin Edge wind-down ends in FY26, so FY27 comps lose that drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock trades on: raise to +12% (Apr 2026) +13.37%; raise to +22% plus FY27 prelim +30% (Jul 2026) +25.13%; full-year guide held (Jan 2026) -13.78%; first FY26 guide (Oct 2025) -16.02%.
findings.why_not_priced: FY27 consensus EPS ($3.38) still equals the company's July number exactly and revenue ($2.21B) is barely above it, so estimates have not been rolled forward for the post-July pricing; the stock is $59 against ~$78 when the prelim was given. Partly priced: Rosenblatt's Oct 2 'expects a raise' note and an +11.6% day (https://koalagains.com/daily-top-movers/top-gainers/details/6d89fc34-3a36-499c-a451-239785f01c6d) and the upside-bid skew say the market expects something above 30%.
findings.independence: TrendForce 4Q26 (https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260930-13258.html, 2026-09-30); Micron FQ4-26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723125/000072312526000018/a2026q4ex991-pressrelease.htm) and reaction coverage (https://finviz.com/news/397848/micron-technology-stock-slides-despite-blowout-q4-report); Dell Q2 FY27 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001571996/000157199626000039/exhibit991earnings8kq2fy27.htm). Shares the Q3 prepared-remarks document with finding 1, but lands on a different line. Counter: the same document warns higher memory costs 'may slow customer demand' and lower margins, and the interim CFO may guide conservatively.

findings.finding: The July 17 $750M 0% convertible (conversion price $116.70, capped call to $175.05) retired $295.5M of 2.00% 2029/2030 notes (cash at par plus ~8.7M shares for the in-the-money excess) and repaid the $100M term loan, leaving roughly $290M of extra cash for a working-capital build (inventory $498M vs $184M a year ago, Q3 operating cash flow -$75M); the coupon and term-loan interest removed (~$10-13M a year pre-tax, ~$0.15 a share) postdates the July 7 FY27 prelim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The convert pricing week coincided with a slide from ~$78 (July 14) to $57.47 (July 23) together with the Barclays downgrade; no print-day history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The financing was read as dilution when announced (stock fell); what it buys, lower interest and working capital for a memory ramp the company says is backlog-led, shows up first in the FY27 EPS guide tonight. If priced, FY27 EPS consensus would sit above the $3.38 prelim rather than on it.
findings.independence: Use of proceeds also at https://btw.media/en/penguin-solutions-750m-zero-coupon-convertible-financing; working-capital figures from the Q3 prepared remarks PDF (shared document with findings 1-2). Answer to 'what does the money buy': deleveraging plus inventory and receivables for a memory ramp, so positive/zero, not distress.

findings.finding: Shorts built into the print, 7.08M shares, 14.23% of float, +9.5% m/m at the Sept 15 settlement, 5.4 days to cover, while the 25-delta skew is -23.7 (calls bid) and put/call OI is 0.54: a crowded short against an upside-bid chain on a name whose last guidance raise moved +25%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two of the last three prints moved more than 13% in the direction of the guide; no separate history for squeezes on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public; what is not in the price is the asymmetry it adds if FY27 is raised (5.4 days of cover against a single-session window). Offset: the stock has already run +15.7% in 20 days, part of which may be covering.
findings.independence: Sweep row's Benzinga snapshot 12.13% / 5.4 days (https://benzinga.com/quote/PENG/short-interest); skew and OI from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: The bear case is public and specific: Barclays went Underweight with a $40 target on July 20 arguing earnings are memory pricing, not durable Advanced Computing growth (AC guided -15% to -20% for FY26, hyperscale excluded), and the pace of DRAM price increases is decelerating sharply (+93-98% in 1Q26, +58-63% 2Q26, +13-18% 3Q26, +10-15% 4Q26) with TrendForce citing consumer affordability limits; Micron's own blowout guide drew a flat-to-down reaction on Oct 1, so a memory-led raise may be read as peak-cycle.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 20 downgrade day -8.41%; a guide hold in Jan 2026 during the memory surge: -13.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell ~35% from the July high on this argument and the deceleration is in every TrendForce release. Filed because the second derivative is what a memory-heavy guide will be judged on tonight; sized small against the upside skew and a 14% short.
findings.independence: TrendForce deceleration (https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260703-13134.html; https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260930-13258.html); Micron muted reaction (https://finviz.com/news/397848/micron-technology-stock-slides-despite-blowout-q4-report). Cuts against finding 2 on the same fact set; resolved by keeping both small and letting p_up carry the net.

findings.finding: The FY27 outlook will be given by an interim CFO (Aaron Johnson, since July 9; Nate Olmstead left July 8), and EDGAR shows no 8-K since July 17, so no permanent CFO has been named; a first full-year guide under an interim CFO carries some conservatism risk, and a permanent appointment could be announced with the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO change was announced June 1 with an improved outlook; no reaction attributable to it alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only; the market knows the CFO is interim. Would be visible as a wider FY27 range or a guide pinned to the prelim.
findings.independence: CFO transition in the Q3 prepared remarks PDF and https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260601026524/en/Penguin-Solutions-Announces-CFO-Transition. Proxy/inference.

findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial in size; filed for completeness.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Memory reported-quarter finding cut from +2.0 to +1.2, since this name's quarter alone has not paid (Jan 2026 memory beat with guide hold fell 13.8%); the guidance finding left at +3.0 because guidance is the line this stock has paid on.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs broad series): kept the ADATA module-maker series below the contract-price series in the Memory sizing; both filed, both labelled proxies.
Lesson 7 (sign against strong skew / crowded short): Barclays/deceleration negative cut from -1.0 to -0.6 and interim-CFO inference from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): convert finding signed positive after answering what the money buys (deleveraging and working capital for a backlog-led memory ramp); unchanged at +0.5.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources; no cap needed. Scaled number (abs 17, p_up 58) unchanged.
